claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lv et al., 2016.

claims.claim: In renal cell carcinoma, Amot is crucial for YAP transcriptional activity by promoting its nuclear localization.
claims.source: Further evidence demonstrated that in renal cell carcinoma (RCC), Amot promotes the proliferation of renal epithelial and RCC cells, and is crucial for YAP transcriptional activity by promoting its nuclear localization (Lv et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lv et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Amot functions as a negative regulator of YAP activity, as direct association of Amot and YAP results in translocation to cytoplasm/cell junctions.
claims.source: However, it has also been reported that Amot functions as a negative regulator of YAP activity, as direct association of Amot and YAP results in translocation to cytoplasm/cell junctions (Leung and Zernicka-Goetz, 2013; Zhao et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Leung and Zernicka-Goetz, 2013 and Zhao et al., 2011.

claims.claim: Amot acts as a scaffold protein to promote localization of YAP, as well as other Hippo/YAP core kinases, to the cytoplasm/cell junctions/actin cytoskeleton and promote Lats1/2-mediated phosphorylation of YAP.
claims.source: Moreover, a number of studies suggest that Amot acts as a scaffold protein to promote localization of YAP, as well as other Hippo/YAP core kinases, to the cytoplasm/cell junctions/actin cytoskeleton and promote Lats1/2-mediated phosphorylation of YAP (Chan et al., 2011; Dai et al., 2013; Paramasivam et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Chan et al., 2011; Dai et al., 2013; Paramasivam et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2011.

claims.claim: Phosphorylation of Ser175 on human Amot (corresponding to Ser176 in mouse) at the conserved HVRSLS motif by Lats1/2 has been reported as a key post-translational modification controlling Amot function and association with YAP.
claims.source: Phosphorylation of Ser175 on human Amot (corresponding to Ser176 in mouse) at the conserved HVRSLS motif by Lats1/2 has been reported as a key post-translational modification controlling Amot function and association with YAP (Hirate et al., 2013; Moleirinho et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hirate et al., 2013 and Moleirinho et al., 2014.

claims.claim: Amot-p130 functions as a scaffold protein mediating YAP and Merlin association.
claims.source: Here we show that Amot-p130 functions as a scaffold protein mediating YAP and Merlin association and that phosphorylation of Amot at Ser176 induces translocation of the complex from the cytoplasm and nucleus to the plasma membrane.
claims.evidence: The claim is stated as a finding from the current study.

claims.claim: Phosphorylation of Amot at Ser176 induces translocation of the Amot/YAP/Merlin complex from the cytoplasm and nucleus to the plasma membrane.
claims.source: Here we show that Amot-p130 functions as a scaffold protein mediating YAP and Merlin association and that phosphorylation of Amot at Ser176 induces translocation of the complex from the cytoplasm and nucleus to the plasma membrane.
claims.evidence: The claim is stated as a finding from the current study.

claims.claim: Relocalization of the Amot/YAP/Merlin complex to the plasma membrane significantly impacts the activity of YAP and regulates YAP's ability to promote cell proliferation and tumorigenesis.
claims.source: This relocalization of the Amot/YAP/Merlin complex significantly impacts the activity of YAP and regulates YAP's ability to promote cell proliferation and tumorigenesis.
claims.evidence: The claim is stated as a finding from the current study.

claims.claim: YAP associates with Merlin in HEK293 cells.
claims.source: First, to determine the interaction between Merlin and YAP, HEK293 cells were transfected with expression vectors for HA-tagged Merlin and V5-tagged YAP. Reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) analyses using anti-HA or anti-V5 antibodies revealed association between YAP and Merlin (Figure 1A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 1A.

claims.claim: The Merlin-YAP interaction was confirmed in hSC2λ immortalized human Schwann cells.
claims.source: The Merlin-YAP interaction was also confirmed in another independent cell type – the hSC2λ immortalized human Schwann cells (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: The association between YAP and Merlin was confirmed at the endogenous protein levels.
claims.source: Importantly, further validation of the association between YAP and Merlin was confirmed at the endogenous protein levels, using antibodies directed against Merlin or YAP (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments with endogenous proteins shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: YAP associates with Merlin primarily in the nucleus and cytoplasm, and to a much lesser extent at the plasma membrane.
claims.source: These subcellular fractionation studies showed an association between Merlin and YAP primarily in the nucleus and cytoplasm, and to a much lesser extent at the plasma membrane (Figure 1D–E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by subcellular fractionation and co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 1D-E.

claims.claim: Merlin and YAP co-localize predominantly in the cytoplasm and nucleus as shown by immunofluorescence.
claims.source: Further confirmation of Merlin and YAP co-localization was provided by immunofluorescence (IF) staining, in HEK293 and hSC2λ cells, where we observed co-localization of IF signal predominantly in the cytoplasm and nucleus (Figure 1F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence experiments shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: In the absence of Amot, YAP and Merlin could no longer be co-immunoprecipitated.
claims.source: Co-IP experiments with HA-tagged Merlin and V5-tagged YAP confirmed that in the absence of Amot, the complex is not formed as YAP and Merlin could no longer be co-immunoprecipitated (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments in Amot knockdown cells shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Knockdown of Amot using an siRNA smartpool impaired the association of Merlin and YAP.
claims.source: Similarly, knockdown of Amot using an siRNA smartpool impaired the association of Merlin and YAP (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments with siRNA knockdown shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Amot-p80 was unable to support the association between Merlin and YAP.
claims.source: As expected, attempting to IP HA-Merlin or V5-YAP demonstrated that Amot-p80 was unable to support the association between these proteins (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments with Amot-p80 shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Mutation of the individual PPEY/LPTY motifs or combinations thereof, significantly impaired the association between Merlin and YAP.
claims.source: Moreover, mutation of the individual PPEY/LPTY motifs or combinations thereof, significantly impaired the association between Merlin and YAP (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments with Amot mutants shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: All three forms of Amot (wild-type, S176A, and S176E) support the formation of the Amot/YAP/Merlin complex.
claims.source: These analyses demonstrated that all three forms of Amot support the formation of the complex, as evidenced by the co-IP of Merlin and YAP (Figure 3A–C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 3A-C.

claims.claim: Amot phosphorylated at S176 binds to both YAP and Merlin.
claims.source: In addition, we examined whether phosphorylated Amot is still able to bind both YAP and Merlin, by using an antibody that specifically binds phosphorylated S176 (p-S176). The antibody was used to IP phosphorylated Amot and co-IP of Merlin and YAP was assessed by western blotting. These experiments showed that Amot phosphorylated at S176 binds to both YAP and Merlin.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments using a phospho-specific antibody.

claims.claim: IP with antibodies against YAP or Merlin showed co-IP with phosphorylated Amot.
claims.source: Similarly, IP with antibodies against YAP or Merlin also showed co-IP with phosphorylated Amot (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: Amot S176 phosphorylation state does not affect formation of the Amot/YAP/Merlin complex.
claims.source: Collectively, our findings demonstrate that Amot S176 phosphorylation state does not affect formation of the Amot/YAP/Merlin complex.
claims.evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the co-immunoprecipitation experiments with different Amot phosphorylation states.

claims.claim: Both phosphorylated YAP and constitutively active YAPS127A mutant retain their ability to associate with Amot/Merlin.
claims.source: Using similar IP approaches described above, we found that both phosphorylated YAP and constitutively active YAPS127A mutant retain their ability to associate with Amot/Merlin (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: A YAP mutant where five major phosphorylation sites have been abolished (YAP-5A) was no longer associated with the Amot-Merlin complex.
claims.source: Surprisingly, a YAP mutant where five major phosphorylation sites have been abolished (YAP-5A [Zhao et al., 2010b]) was no longer associated with the complex (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claims.claim: In cells expressing Amot-p130, the majority of this protein localized to cytoplasmic and nuclear fractions, and to a lesser extent in the plasma membrane fraction.
claims.source: In the cells expressing Amot-p130, the majority of this protein localized to cytoplasmic and nuclear fractions, and to a lesser extent in the plasma membrane fraction.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by subcellular fractionation experiments.

claims.claim: Amot-p130S176A showed a marked increase in nuclear localization and almost no presence at the plasma membrane.
claims.source: Interestingly, Amot-p130S176A showed a marked increase in nuclear localization and almost no presence at the plasma membrane.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by subcellular fractionation experiments.

claims.claim: Amot-p130S176E showed a clear shift in localization towards the cytoplasm and plasma membrane.
claims.source: In contrast, Amot-p130S176E showed a clear shift in localization towards the cytoplasm and plasma membrane (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by subcellular fractionation experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: Fractionation studies from hSC2λ Schwann cells and HepG2 hepatocellular carcinoma cells followed a similar distribution pattern to the transfected 293-shAmot cells.
claims.source: To determine the broader relevance of our findings in HEK293 cells to additional biological systems, we carried out a similar analysis in human hSC2λ Schwann cells and HepG2 hepatocellular carcinoma cells. Fractionation studies from these additional cell types followed a similar distribution pattern to the transfected 293-shAmot cells (Figure 4—figure supplements 1A and 2A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by subcellular fractionation experiments in additional cell types shown in Figure 4—figure supplements 1A and 2A.

claims.claim: Immunofluorescence analyses confirmed a stronger intensity of Amot in the cytoplasm and nucleus of cells expressing Amot-p130.
claims.source: To complement the biochemical fractionation studies, we assessed localization of the different Amot proteins by IF staining in the 293-shAmot cells. These analyses confirmed the fractionation findings, demonstrating a stronger intensity of Amot in the cytoplasm and nucleus of cells expressing Amot-p130, a shift to nuclear staining in Amot-p130S176A expressing cells and cytoplasmic/plasma membrane localization in Amot-p130S176E expressing cells (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: Immunofluorescence showed a shift to nuclear staining in Amot-p130S176A expressing cells.
claims.source: To complement the biochemical fractionation studies, we assessed localization of the different Amot proteins by IF staining in the 293-shAmot cells. These analyses confirmed the fractionation findings, demonstrating a stronger intensity of Amot in the cytoplasm and nucleus of cells expressing Amot-p130, a shift to nuclear staining in Amot-p130S176A expressing cells and cytoplasmic/plasma membrane localization in Amot-p130S176E expressing cells (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: Immunofluorescence showed cytoplasmic/plasma membrane localization in Amot-p130S176E expressing cells.
claims.source: To complement the biochemical fractionation studies, we assessed localization of the different Amot proteins by IF staining in the 293-shAmot cells. These analyses confirmed the fractionation findings, demonstrating a stronger intensity of Amot in the cytoplasm and nucleus of cells expressing Amot-p130, a shift to nuclear staining in Amot-p130S176A expressing cells and cytoplasmic/plasma membrane localization in Amot-p130S176E expressing cells (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: In 293-shAmot cells transfected with Amot-p130 and YAP, Amot co-IPed with YAP mainly in the cytoplasm but also in the nucleus with little to no interaction detected at the plasma membrane.
claims.source: In agreement with our previous results, in 293-shAmot cells transfected with Amot-p130 and YAP, Amot co-IPed with YAP mainly in the cytoplasm but also in the nucleus with little to no interaction detected at the plasma membrane (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments in subcellular fractions shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: In cells expressing the Amot-p130S176A allele, the Amot-YAP complex mainly localized to the nucleus with little to no interaction detected in the cytoplasm and plasma membrane.
claims.source: Importantly, in cells expressing the Amot-p130S176A allele, the Amot-YAP complex mainly localized to the nucleus with little to no interaction detected in the cytoplasm and plasma membrane (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments in subcellular fractions shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: In cells expressing the Amot-p130S176E allele an increase in the Amot-YAP association was detected at the plasma membrane, in addition to the cytoplasmic fraction, with little to no interaction detected in the nucleus.
claims.source: Significantly, in cells expressing the Amot-p130S176E allele an increase in the Amot-YAP association was detected at the plasma membrane, in addition to the cytoplasmic fraction. Little to no interaction was detected in the nucleus (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments in subcellular fractions shown in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: The distribution of Amot/YAP complex mimics the distribution observed for Amot.
claims.source: Thus, the distribution of Amot/YAP complex mimics the distribution observed for Amot (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from comparing the distribution patterns of Amot and the Amot/YAP complex.

claims.claim: Immunofluorescence analysis showed the localization of YAP and Merlin to the plasma membrane is significantly enhanced in cells expressing the Amot-p130S176E allele.
claims.source: These findings were extended and confirmed by IF analysis of the YAP-Merlin association in 293-shAmot cells, where the localization of YAP and Merlin to the plasma membrane is significantly enhanced in cells expressing the Amot-p130S176E allele (Figure 4G).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence experiments shown in Figure 4G.

claims.claim: AmotS176 phosphorylation does not impact the formation of the Amot/YAP/Merlin complex, but mediates the localization of the complex.
claims.source: Overall our findings demonstrate that while AmotS176 phosphorylation does not impact the formation of the Amot/YAP/Merlin complex, it mediates the localization of the complex through phosphorylation of Serine 176 that leads to recruitment of the complex to the plasma membrane or a shift to a nuclear localization in the hypophosphorylated state.
claims.evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the co-immunoprecipitation and localization experiments.

claims.claim: Phosphorylation of Serine 176 leads to recruitment of the Amot/YAP/Merlin complex to the plasma membrane.
claims.source: Overall our findings demonstrate that while AmotS176 phosphorylation does not impact the formation of the Amot/YAP/Merlin complex, it mediates the localization of the complex through phosphorylation of Serine 176 that leads to recruitment of the complex to the plasma membrane or a shift to a nuclear localization in the hypophosphorylated state.
claims.evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the co-immunoprecipitation and localization experiments.

claims.claim: Hypophosphorylation of Amot at Serine 176 leads to a shift to nuclear localization of the Amot/YAP/Merlin complex.
claims.source: Overall our findings demonstrate that while AmotS176 phosphorylation does not impact the formation of the Amot/YAP/Merlin complex, it mediates the localization of the complex through phosphorylation of Serine 176 that leads to recruitment of the complex to the plasma membrane or a shift to a nuclear localization in the hypophosphorylated state.
claims.evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the co-immunoprecipitation and localization experiments.

claims.claim: Flag-tagged Patj strongly associates with Amot-p130S176E, compared to weaker or null interaction with Amot-p130 and Amot-p130S176A, respectively.
claims.source: Using co-IP, we found that Flag-tagged Patj strongly associates with Amot-p130S176E, compared to weaker or null interaction with Amot-p130 and Amot-p130S176A, respectively.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments.

claims.claim: IP of the different Amot forms demonstrated a stronger association between Patj and Amot-p130S176E.
claims.source: In a reciprocal approach, IP of the different Amot forms demonstrated a stronger association between Patj and Amot-p130S176E (Figure 5A–C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 5A-C.

claims.claim: Pals1 was consistently able to co-IP with Amot-p130S176E, but this association was greatly diminished with Amot-p130S176A or wild type Amot-p130.
claims.source: Similar results were obtained when examining the association of Pals1 or E-cadherin with Amot. While we were consistently able to co-IP Pals1 or E-cadherin with Amot-p130S176E, this association was greatly diminished with Amot-p130S176A or wild type Amot-p130 (Figure 5D–E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 5D-E.

claims.claim: E-cadherin was consistently able to co-IP with Amot-p130S176E, but this association was greatly diminished with Amot-p130S176A or wild type Amot-p130.
claims.source: Similar results were obtained when examining the association of Pals1 or E-cadherin with Amot. While we were consistently able to co-IP Pals1 or E-cadherin with Amot-p130S176E, this association was greatly diminished with Amot-p130S176A or wild type Amot-p130 (Figure 5D–E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 5D-E.

claims.claim: Localization of phosphorylated Amot-p130 to the cell membrane is mediated through interactions with components of junctional structures.
claims.source: These findings suggest that localization of phosphorylated Amot-p130 to the cell membrane is mediated through interactions with components of junctional structures, which remain to be identified.
claims.evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the co-immunoprecipitation experiments showing association with junctional proteins.

claims.claim: Similar amounts of all Amot proteins (wild-type, S176A, and S176E) were present in F-actin pull downs.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 5F, similar amounts of all Amot proteins were present in the pull downs (Upper panel).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by F-actin pull-down experiments shown in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: Similar levels of Actin were present in all pull downs indicating the expression of the different Amot alleles did not affect cellular levels of F-actin.
claims.source: Importantly, similar levels of Actin were present in all pull downs indicating the expression of the different Amot alleles did not affect cellular levels of F-actin (Lower panel).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by F-actin pull-down experiments shown in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: 293-shAmot cells transfected with expression plasmids for Amot-p130 and Amot-p130S176A proliferated at increased rates compared to control transfected cells.
claims.source: The 293-shAmot cells transfected with expression plasmids for Amot-p130 and Amot-p130S176A proliferated at increased rates compared to control transfected cells, as determined by cell counting and BrdU incorporation over a 96 hr period.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by cell counting and BrdU incorporation assays.

claims.claim: Amot-p130S176E expressing cells exhibited a growth rate comparable to that of the control cells.
claims.source: In contrast, the Amot-p130S176E expressing cells exhibited a growth rate comparable to that of the control cells (Figure 6A–B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by cell counting and BrdU incorporation assays shown in Figure 6A-B.

claims.claim: Similar results were obtained in hSC2λ and HepG2 cells transfected with the different Amot alleles.
claims.source: Similar results were obtained in hSC2λ and HepG2 cells transfected with the different Amot alleles (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by cell counting experiments in additional cell types shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-B.

claims.claim: Expression of Amot can promote the proliferation of HEK293, hSC2λ, and HepG2 cells and this activity is diminished when Amot is phosphorylated at Serine 176.
claims.source: These findings indicate that expression of Amot can promote the proliferation of these three different cell types and that this activity is diminished when Amot is phosphorylated at Serine 176.
claims.evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the cell proliferation experiments.

claims.claim: Transfection with the different Amot alleles resulted in increased Rac1-GTP levels.
claims.source: As expected, transfection with the different Amot alleles resulted in increased Rac1-GTP levels.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by Rac1-GTP pull-down assays.

claims.claim: No significant differences in Rac1-GTP levels were found between cells expressing different Amot alleles, suggesting the status of Amot serine 176 phosphorylation does not affect Rac1 activation.
claims.source: However, we found no significant differences in Rac1-GTP levels between the cells, suggesting the status of Amot serine 176 phosphorylation does not affect Rac1 activation (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by Rac1-GTP pull-down assays shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: The increased proliferation afforded by Amot-p130 and Amot-p130S176A was completely inhibited by YAP knockdown.
claims.source: Indeed, the increased proliferation afforded by Amot-p130 and Amot-p130S176A was completely inhibited by YAP knockdown (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU incorporation assays with YAP knockdown shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: The activity of YAP in the HOP-reporter assay was suppressed in 293-shAmot cells.
claims.source: In agreement with our previously reported findings (Yi et al., 2013), the activity of YAP in the HOP-reporter assay was suppressed in 293-shAmot cells, while the reintroduction of Amot fully rescued YAP activity (Figure 6D–E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assays shown in Figure 6D-E and a citation to Yi et al., 2013.

claims.claim: Reintroduction of Amot fully rescued YAP activity in 293-shAmot cells.
claims.source: In agreement with our previously reported findings (Yi et al., 2013), the activity of YAP in the HOP-reporter assay was suppressed in 293-shAmot cells, while the reintroduction of Amot fully rescued YAP activity (Figure 6D–E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assays shown in Figure 6D-E and a citation to Yi et al., 2013.

claims.claim: Expression of Amot-p130S176A resulted in a substantial increase in the activation of the HOP-flash reporter when compared to Amot.
claims.source: Moreover, the expression of Amot-p130S176A resulted in a substantial increase in the activation of the HOP-flash reporter when compared to Amot.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assays.

claims.claim: Amot-p130S176E was unable to rescue the function of YAP in the 293-shAmot cells.
claims.source: Significantly, Amot-p130S176E was unable to rescue the function of YAP in the 293-shAmot cells (Figure 6D–E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assays shown in Figure 6D-E.

claims.claim: No significant changes in activation of the HIP reporter were observed under similar experimental conditions.
claims.source: As expected, no significant changes in activation of the HIP reporter were observed under similar experimental conditions (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assays shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: Expression of both Amot-p130 and Amot-p130S176E had only minor effects on levels of Areg and ApoE.
claims.source: While expression of both Amot-p130 and Amot-p130S176E had only minor effects on levels of Areg and ApoE, the expression of Amot-p130S176A significantly induced up-regulation of Areg and ApoE by 2.5, and 3-fold respectively, relative to control cells (Figure 6F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative real-time PCR experiments shown in Figure 6F.

claims.claim: Expression of Amot-p130S176A significantly induced up-regulation of Areg and ApoE by 2.5, and 3-fold respectively, relative to control cells.
claims.source: While expression of both Amot-p130 and Amot-p130S176E had only minor effects on levels of Areg and ApoE, the expression of Amot-p130S176A significantly induced up-regulation of Areg and ApoE by 2.5, and 3-fold respectively, relative to control cells (Figure 6F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative real-time PCR experiments shown in Figure 6F.

claims.claim: Similar results were obtained in hSC2λ and HepG2 cells transfected with the different Amot alleles for Areg and ApoE expression.
claims.source: Similar results were obtained in hSC2λ and HepG2 cells transfected with the different Amot alleles (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative real-time PCR experiments in additional cell types shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: Amot is part of transcriptionally active YAP-Tead-containing complex in the nuclei of adult liver and HEK293 cells.
claims.source: Previously it was shown that Amot is part of transcriptionally active YAP-Tead-containing complex in the nuclei of adult liver and HEK293 cells (Yi et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yi et al., 2013.

claims.claim: Efficient co-IP of YAP and pan-Tead was observed in the presence of Amot-p130 and Amot-p130S176A but not in the presence of Amot-p130S176E.
claims.source: To test this, we performed reciprocal IP assays with antibodies against YAP or pan-Tead. We observed efficient co-IP of YAP and pan-Tead in the presence of Amot-p130 and Amot-p130S176A but not in the presence of Amot-p130S176E (Figure 7A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: ChIP experiments showed a striking enrichment and binding of Amot-p130S176A to the promoter of ApoE and Areg, compared to Amot.
claims.source: Moreover, we conducted Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) with Amot antibodies in 293-shAmot cells transfected with Amot-p130, Amot-p130S176A or an empty control vector, followed by RT-PCR analysis. These experiments showed a striking enrichment and binding of Amot-p130S176A to the promoter of ApoE and Areg, compared to Amot (Figure 7B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP experiments shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: Phosphorylation of Amot serine 176 prevents YAP-mediated transcriptional activation by inhibiting Amot nuclear function as a co-factor in a YAP-Tead transcriptional complex.
claims.source: These findings suggest that phosphorylation of Amot serine 176 prevents YAP-mediated transcriptional activation by inhibiting Amot nuclear function as a co-factor in a YAP-Tead transcriptional complex (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the co-immunoprecipitation and ChIP experiments, and is illustrated in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: Hypophosphorylation of AmotS176 promotes translocation of the Amot-p130/YAP/Merlin complex from the cytoplasm to the nucleus where it binds to TEADs and activates YAP-dependent transcriptional programs.
claims.source: Hypophosphorylation of AmotS176 promotes translocation of the Amot-p130/YAP/Merlin complex from the cytoplasm to the nucleus where it binds to TEADs and activates YAP-dependent transcriptional programs.
claims.evidence: The claim is stated in the proposed model shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: Phosphorylation of AmotS176 induces cytoplasmic sequestration and plasma membrane localization of the tertiary complex.
claims.source: Conversely, phosphorylation of AmotS176 induces cytoplasmic sequestration and plasma membrane localization of the tertiary complex.
claims.evidence: The claim is stated in the proposed model shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: At the membrane, the Amot/YAP/Merlin complex associates with the junctional proteins Patj and Pals1 and YAP's nuclear functions are inhibited.
claims.source: At the membrane, the complex associates with the junctional proteins Patj and Pals1 and YAP's nuclear functions are inhibited.
claims.evidence: The claim is stated in the proposed model shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: Angiomotin phosphorylation at serine 176 mediates YAP localization.
claims.source: Our study reveals that Angiomotin phosphorylation at serine 176 mediates YAP localization.
claims.evidence: The claim is stated as a main finding in the Discussion section.

claims.claim: Phosphorylation at serine 176 is the key event determining a promoting or repressing regulation of YAP by Angiomotin.
claims.source: This post-translational modification is the key event determining a promoting or repressing regulation of YAP by Angiomotin.
claims.evidence: The claim is stated as a main finding in the Discussion section.

claims.claim: Phosphorylation at serine 176 does not mediate Angiomotin's scaffolding functions but does impact the localization of a tertiary complex composed by Amot, YAP and Merlin.
claims.source: We found that phosphorylation at serine 176 does not mediate Angiomotin's scaffolding functions but does impact the localization of a tertiary complex composed by Amot, YAP and Merlin, which is present in both the cytoplasm and nucleus for the wild type protein.
claims.evidence: The claim is stated as a main finding in the Discussion section.

claims.claim: The serine 176 phosphomimetic mutant (AmotS176E) is recruited to the plasma membrane where it is found co-localized and associated with Patj, Pals1 and E-cadherin at junctional structures.
claims.source: The serine 176 phosphomimetic mutant (AmotS176E) is recruited to the plasma membrane where it is found co-localized and associated with Patj, Pals1 and E-cadherin at junctional structures.
claims.evidence: The claim is stated as a main finding in the Discussion section.

claims.claim: Amot is required for YAP function in the nucleus.
claims.source: Our previous studies indicate that Amot is required for YAP function in the nucleus (Yi et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yi et al., 2013.

claims.claim: The relocation of Amot out of the nucleus and sequestration of Amot/YAP complex to the plasma membrane function to prevent YAP from operating as a growth-promoting transcriptional activator.

results.result: YAP and Merlin form a complex that localizes primarily to the nucleus and cytoplasm. This was demonstrated through co-immunoprecipitation experiments in HEK293 and hSC2λ cells using both overexpressed and endogenous proteins, and confirmed by subcellular fractionation and immunofluorescence showing predominant co-localization in cytoplasm and nucleus with minimal plasma membrane association.
results.evaluation: Multiple independent experimental approaches (co-IP with tagged proteins, endogenous co-IP, subcellular fractionation, and immunofluorescence) consistently demonstrate YAP-Merlin association primarily in nucleus and cytoplasm across two cell types (C36-C40). The convergence of biochemical and imaging data provides strong support.

results.result: Amot-p130 functions as a scaffold protein required for YAP-Merlin complex formation. Knockdown of Amot abolishes YAP-Merlin co-immunoprecipitation, and the truncated Amot-p80 isoform lacking the N-terminal PPxY/LPTY motifs cannot support complex formation. Mutation of these motifs significantly impairs YAP-Merlin association.
results.evaluation: The scaffolding role is well-supported by loss-of-function experiments (shRNA and siRNA knockdown) showing loss of YAP-Merlin interaction (C41-C42), and structure-function studies with Amot-p80 and motif mutants demonstrating requirement for N-terminal binding domains (C43-C44). The data logically establish Amot as a necessary scaffold.

results.result: Amot S176 phosphorylation does not affect formation of the Amot/YAP/Merlin complex. All three forms of Amot (wild-type, S176A non-phosphorylatable, and S176E phosphomimetic) support complex formation, and phosphorylated Amot (detected with phospho-specific antibody) co-immunoprecipitates with both YAP and Merlin.
results.evaluation: Co-IP experiments with all three Amot variants (C45) and phospho-specific antibody experiments (C46-C47) consistently show complex formation independent of S176 phosphorylation status. The use of phospho-specific antibodies provides direct evidence that phosphorylated Amot remains in complex with YAP and Merlin (C48).

results.result: Amot S176 phosphorylation regulates subcellular localization of Amot. Wild-type Amot-p130 localizes to cytoplasm and nucleus with minimal plasma membrane presence. The S176A mutant shows marked nuclear enrichment with almost no plasma membrane localization, while the S176E phosphomimetic shows a shift toward cytoplasm and plasma membrane. This pattern was confirmed in HEK293, hSC2λ, and HepG2 cells by both fractionation and immunofluorescence.
results.evaluation: The localization shift is demonstrated by two independent methods (subcellular fractionation C51-C54 and immunofluorescence C55-C57) across three cell types. The consistent pattern where S176A is nuclear and S176E is membrane-localized provides strong evidence that phosphorylation at this site controls Amot localization.

results.result: Amot S176 phosphorylation controls the subcellular localization of the Amot/YAP/Merlin complex. The distribution of the complex mirrors Amot localization: with wild-type Amot, the complex is mainly cytoplasmic/nuclear; with S176A, it is predominantly nuclear; with S176E, it shifts to plasma membrane and cytoplasm. Immunofluorescence confirms enhanced YAP and Merlin plasma membrane localization with Amot-S176E.
results.evaluation: Co-IP from subcellular fractions (C58-C60) directly demonstrates that the Amot/YAP complex distribution follows Amot localization patterns. The parallel between Amot alone and Amot/YAP complex distribution (C61) and IF confirmation (C62) support the conclusion that S176 phosphorylation controls complex localization (C63-C65).

results.result: Phosphorylated Amot (S176E) preferentially associates with junctional proteins. Amot-S176E shows strong association with Patj, Pals1, and E-cadherin compared to weak or absent interaction with wild-type Amot-p130 and Amot-S176A, suggesting that phosphorylation-dependent membrane localization is mediated through interactions with junctional components.
results.evaluation: Reciprocal co-IP experiments consistently show preferential binding of junctional proteins (Patj, Pals1, E-cadherin) to Amot-S176E versus other forms (C66-C69). While the specific mechanism remains to be identified (C70), the differential binding pattern provides strong evidence for phosphorylation-dependent junctional protein recruitment.

results.result: Amot S176 phosphorylation does not affect F-actin binding. F-actin pull-down experiments show similar amounts of all Amot variants (wild-type, S176A, S176E) associate with F-actin, and similar F-actin levels across conditions indicate no effect on cellular F-actin content.
results.evaluation: The phalloidin-based F-actin pull-down assay directly tests binding and shows equivalent recovery of all Amot forms (C71). The control showing equal F-actin levels (C72) rules out indirect effects through altered actin polymerization. This contradicts some prior reports but is supported by the direct biochemical evidence presented.

results.result: Amot-p130 and Amot-S176A promote cell proliferation, while Amot-S176E does not. In HEK293-shAmot, hSC2λ, and HepG2 cells, expression of Amot-p130 or S176A increased proliferation rates compared to controls, while S176E-expressing cells showed growth rates comparable to controls, indicating that S176 phosphorylation diminishes Amot's pro-proliferative activity.
results.evaluation: Cell counting and BrdU incorporation assays across three cell types consistently show increased proliferation with Amot-p130 and S176A but not S176E (C73-C75). The reproducibility across cell types and assay methods supports the conclusion that S176 phosphorylation negatively regulates Amot's proliferative function (C76).

results.result: Amot S176 phosphorylation status does not affect Rac1 activation. While all Amot alleles increased Rac1-GTP levels compared to controls, no significant differences were observed between wild-type, S176A, and S176E forms.
results.evaluation: Rac1-GTP pull-down assays show equivalent activation across Amot variants (C77-C78). This indicates that the differential proliferative effects of S176 phosphorylation are not mediated through Rac1 signaling, helping to narrow the mechanism of action.

results.result: The pro-proliferative effects of Amot-p130 and Amot-S176A are YAP-dependent. YAP knockdown completely abolished the increased proliferation induced by Amot-p130 and Amot-S176A expression.
results.evaluation: The genetic epistasis experiment using YAP knockdown (C79) directly demonstrates YAP requirement for Amot-mediated proliferation. This establishes YAP as a necessary downstream effector and links the proliferative phenotype to the YAP pathway.

results.result: Amot S176 phosphorylation regulates YAP transcriptional activity. In HOP-flash reporter assays, YAP activity was suppressed in Amot-depleted cells and rescued by Amot-p130 reintroduction. Amot-S176A showed substantially increased reporter activation compared to wild-type, while Amot-S176E failed to rescue YAP activity. No changes were observed in the negative control HIP reporter.
results.evaluation: The luciferase reporter assays show a clear pattern: S176A enhances YAP activity, wild-type partially rescues, and S176E fails to rescue (C80-C83). The specificity is confirmed by lack of effect on the HIP control reporter (C84). This directly links S176 phosphorylation to YAP transcriptional output.

results.result: Amot-S176A specifically upregulates YAP target genes. Expression of Amot-S176A significantly induced Areg and ApoE mRNA levels (2.5- and 3-fold, respectively) in HEK293-shAmot, hSC2λ, and HepG2 cells, while Amot-p130 and Amot-S176E had minimal effects.
results.evaluation: qRT-PCR analysis of endogenous YAP target genes across three cell types consistently shows specific upregulation by S176A but not other forms (C85-C87). This complements the reporter assays and demonstrates effects on endogenous gene expression, strengthening the conclusion about S176 regulation of YAP activity.

results.result: Amot S176 phosphorylation prevents YAP-TEAD interaction and chromatin binding. Co-IP experiments show efficient YAP-TEAD association with Amot-p130 and S176A but not S176E. ChIP experiments demonstrate striking enrichment of Amot-S176A at ApoE and Areg promoters compared to wild-type Amot, suggesting that S176 phosphorylation inhibits Amot's nuclear co-factor function in the YAP-TEAD transcriptional complex.
results.evaluation: The co-IP data (C89) show S176E disrupts YAP-TEAD interaction, and ChIP data (C90) show enhanced S176A binding to target gene promoters. Together, these provide mechanistic insight into how S176 phosphorylation regulates YAP transcriptional activity (C91). The convergence of protein interaction and chromatin binding data is compelling.

results.result: YAP phosphorylation at S127 does not affect Amot/Merlin complex formation, but the YAP-5A mutant (with five phosphorylation sites abolished) fails to associate with the complex. Both phosphorylated YAP and constitutively active YAPS127A retain ability to bind Amot/Merlin.
results.evaluation: While the data clearly show S127 phosphorylation is not required for complex formation (C49), the surprising loss of binding with YAP-5A (C50) suggests at least one of the five sites is important. However, the specific site(s) and mechanism remain unidentified. The authors acknowledge this requires future investigation, making the result incomplete.

results.result: Background information on Angiomotin family proteins, Hippo-YAP pathway, and conflicting reports about Amot's role in YAP regulation. This includes Amot's structure and isoforms, functions in cell migration and polarity, the core Hippo-YAP signaling cascade, YAP's role in cancer, and previous contradictory findings showing Amot as both positive and negative regulator of YAP.
results.evaluation: These claims represent established knowledge from prior literature, appropriately cited throughout (C1-C32). They provide necessary context for the current study but are not novel findings. The citations appear appropriate and the background accurately represents the field's understanding and controversies.

results.result: Summary and model: Amot-p130 scaffolds YAP-Merlin complex formation, and S176 phosphorylation is the key regulatory switch determining whether Amot promotes or represses YAP activity by controlling complex localization. Hypophosphorylated Amot promotes nuclear translocation and YAP-TEAD transcriptional activation, while phosphorylated Amot induces plasma membrane sequestration with junctional proteins and inhibits YAP nuclear function.
results.evaluation: These claims synthesize the major findings into a coherent model (C33-C35, C92-C97, C141-C142). The model is well-supported by the collective experimental evidence showing: (1) Amot scaffolds the complex, (2) S176 phosphorylation controls localization without affecting complex formation, (3) localization determines YAP activity, and (4) this explains previous contradictory reports. The model integrates all major results logically.

results.result: Discussion of findings in context of prior literature, including comparison with conflicting reports about Amot S176 phosphorylation effects, speculation about regulatory mechanisms involving Lats1/2 and other kinases, and discussion of Merlin's nuclear function. The authors acknowledge cell-type differences and call for in vivo validation.
results.evaluation: These discussion claims (C99-C140) include a mix of well-supported interpretations, reasonable speculation, and acknowledged uncertainties. The comparison with prior literature is appropriate (C105-C115), but many mechanistic details remain speculative (C119, C130, C133-C134). The call for in vivo studies (C116) acknowledges limitations. The discussion appropriately contextualizes findings but contains substantial speculation.
